form_analysis.feedback: Excellent aftercare form for general permanent makeup removal encompassing various cosmetic tattoos. Comprehensive guidance on facial area considerations, color-specific risks, and correction approaches. Strong emphasis on the cosmetic implications and realistic outcomes.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser removal of various PERMANENT MAKEUP (cosmetic tattoos): eyeliner, eyebrow, lip, beauty marks, scalp micropigmentation. Each area has specific considerations. PMU pigments are often iron oxide-based with high titanium dioxide content.

instructions.general_directive: Follow area-specific care. Permanent makeup removal involves both technical and cosmetic considerations.

sections.title: Permanent Makeup Types & Considerations
items: Eyeliner: Close to eyes, risk of corneal injury. Special shields used.
Eyebrows: Hair follicle preservation, shape considerations.
Lips: Herpes risk, swelling, color challenges.
Beauty marks: Small area, complete removal often possible.
Scalp: Large area, multiple sessions, hair protection.

sections.title: Facial Area Considerations
items: Thin facial skin: Higher risk of textural changes.
Cosmetic importance: Asymmetry becomes apparent during removal.
Social implications: Visible during treatment process.
Multiple procedures: May have different pigments from different artists.

sections.title: Color-Specific Risks for PMU
items: Iron oxide pigments: May oxidize to gray/black.
Titanium dioxide (white): Whitens with laser, may require different approach.
Mixed pigments: Unpredictable responses.
Old vs. new PMU: Older pigments often easier to remove.

sections.title: Correction vs. Removal Decision
sections.content: Most PMU removal is for CORRECTION not complete removal: Too dark, wrong color, poor shape, migration. Goal is often 50-70% lightening then new PMU over top. Complete removal may leave hypopigmentation.

sections.title: Realistic PMU Expectations
items: 3-8 sessions depending on pigment, depth, color.
Color may worsen before improving.
Complete removal often not possible without textural changes.
May need combination approaches (laser + saline).
Extended timeline: 1-2 years for complete process.

sections.title: Post-Removal Options
items: New PMU by experienced artist.
Temporary makeup during process.
Camouflage techniques for residual pigment.
Scar management if textural changes occur.
Acceptance of subtle residual color.
